# The suite's rules, in full

SUITE-RULES.md is the one-page list. This is every rule in full, for whoever fixes a failure.

## SR-01 · A story is in cypress/e2e/cases/ (story)

**Why.** One folder holds every story, the generated tests beside them; a spec of your own that is not a story may live anywhere under cypress/e2e/.

**How to fix it.** Move the story's spec into cypress/e2e/cases/ and fix its imports (../../support/...).

## SR-04 · A story's file is named after its id (story)

**Why.** Finding the test of a story, or the story of a test, is then a file name, not a search.

**How to fix it.** Rename the file to the id in lower case: PROJ-1 is proj-1.cy.ts, and its third requirement PROJ-1-3 is proj-1-3.cy.ts (G-188).

## SR-05 · Each story id is used once (story)

**Why.** Two tests for one story (or one requirement of it, PROJ-1-3) report it twice, and the tracker can't tell which one speaks for it.

**How to fix it.** Keep one; give the other its own story and id.

## SR-06 · A story is one test (advisory)

**Why.** One story states one outcome: one story() call, with no it() or describe() of its own beside it.

**How to fix it.** Split a second outcome into a story of its own, in its own file.

## SR-07 · A story has one check (advisory)

**Why.** A story's test proves its one outcome with one .verify() at the end of its chain. Two outcomes are two stories.

**How to fix it.** End the chain with one .verify()...; push back on a story that asks for two outcomes (stories/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md).

## SR-08 · The check comes last (advisory)

**Why.** The check is the story's outcome: a step after it is a second story hiding in the first.

**How to fix it.** Move the step before .verify(), or make what follows a story of its own.

## SR-10 · A story uses page objects, not Cypress (story)

**Why.** A story reads like the story because every step is a page method named for what a visitor does ("click().learnMore()"). Selectors and cy calls in a test hide what it does, break when the site changes in many places at once, and skip the step log the page objects give.

**How to fix it.** Add the element to the page's Elements (ai/recipes/add-an-element.md) and an action or check that uses it (add-an-action.md); call that from the story.

## SR-11 · A story does not assert (advisory)

**Why.** Checks live in the pages' verify() methods, built on Checks, which log the step and fail in plain English. An expect() in a story fails with "expected true", logs nothing, and is a second check SR-07 cannot see.

**How to fix it.** Use (or add) a check in the page's VerifyActions and end the story with it.

## SR-12 · Nothing sleeps (advisory)

**Why.** cy.wait(2000) is slow on a fast day and too short on a slow one. Waiting for what the step needs is both faster and surer.

**How to fix it.** Wait for what the step needs with WaitActions (ai/recipes/wait-for-a-slow-page.md); cy.wait('@alias') for a request is fine.

## SR-13 · No regular expressions in tests and pages (advisory)

**Why.** Expected texts and addresses are plain strings: a person reads them at a glance, and a regular expression that looks right can quietly match the wrong thing.

**How to fix it.** Compare plain strings (Checks.hasText, containsText); what needs more belongs in support/core/.

## SR-14 · A test switched off says why (advisory)

**Why.** A test skipped without a word passes in every report and is forgotten; with its reason on the line, the next person knows whether it can come back. .only silently switches off every other test.

**How to fix it.** Say why on the line (it.skip('...', () => { // search is down: KNOWN-ISSUES.md), or delete a stale test, or fix it; take .only out.

## SR-15 · YOURS blocks keep both marker lines (hard)

**Why.** Regenerating keeps what is between the marker lines: a block missing one of them is lost, or swallows the rest of the file.

**How to fix it.** Put the marker line back, exactly as generated.

## SR-16 · Generated files change only inside YOURS blocks (hard)

**Why.** Everything outside the blocks is rewritten by the next rebuild, the rules included: an edit there is lost.

**How to fix it.** Move the change into a YOURS block, or into a file of your own; suite build &lt;project> puts the rest back. A change to guidance text (a Markdown file that is no rule) is a warning only (G-184): a change worth keeping goes into Suite Builder too.

## SR-17 · Every story in stories/done/ has its test (story)

**Why.** A story marked done without a test is a promise nothing keeps.

**How to fix it.** Write its test (stories/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md), move the story back to stories/new/, or delete it if it is stale.

## SR-18 · Every story test has its story in stories/done/ (story)

**Why.** A test whose story is gone tests something nobody asked for any more, or its story was lost.

**How to fix it.** Add the story file (the story's words, with an IMPLEMENTED note naming this test), or delete the test if the story is stale.

## SR-19 · Every test checks something (hard)

**Why.** A test that only acts passes whenever nothing throws: it can't tell the right page from the wrong one. Even the plainest test ends by saying what it expected, if only that the page it reached has loaded.

**How to fix it.** End the test with .verify()... on the page it reaches, or a Checks call (Checks.assume is not one: it skips a test whose data is not there).

## SR-20 · Account files stay out of git (hard)

**Why.** An account in git is an account everyone with the repository has: the account files in secrets/ are each person's own, written blank in every fresh copy (G-159).

**How to fix it.** Put secrets/*.login back in .gitignore; for a file already committed, git rm --cached it, then change that account's password.

## SR-21 · A done story's notes name every criterion, by its number (story)

**Why.** A criterion's number is its test's name (&lt;id>-&lt;n>): a list edited after its tests were written moves every number after the edit, so a test checks one criterion under another's number, and a criterion left out of the notes is a part of the story nobody checks, or says is unchecked (trial 7: 3 of 3 list edits renumbered tested stories).

**How to fix it.** Implement each criterion named as &lt;id>-&lt;n>, or add a Not implemented line for it to the story's IMPLEMENTED note (&lt;n> &lt;the criterion>: &lt;what is needed>). A list changed after its tests: put it back as it was; a dropped criterion stays in the list, answered "drop" under a Not implemented line.

## SR-22 · One element, one name (hard)

**Why.** Every test then reaches one element two ways, and a locator fixed under one name is still broken under the other; two stories written apart (two branches) each add their own name for the same button and merge without a conflict.

**How to fix it.** Keep one name, delete the other constant, and point every use of it at the one kept (search the tests and pages for its name). Before adding an element, search the Elements for its locator (ai/recipes/add-an-element.md).

## SR-02 · A story is written with story() (holds by how a story is written)

A story is a spec that calls story() (G-119): a spec that does not is a test of your own, held to the hard rules only, so no story is written without it.

## SR-03 · A story names its story (holds by how a story is written)

story('&lt;id>', '&lt;title>', () => ...) cannot be written without the story's id: SR-02, which asks for story(), asks for the id too.

## SR-09 · A story's test reads as its title (holds by how a story is written)

story() names the test with the story's title, so the report and the run's output read as the story.
